act_title: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended by Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023 & Rules 2024)
authority: National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) & State Biodiversity Boards (SBB)

chunks.chapter: Chapter II: Regulation of Access to Biological Diversity
chunks.title: Certain persons not to undertake Biodiversity related activities without approval of National Biodiversity Authority
chunks.legal_text: 1. No person who is: (a) not a citizen of India; (b) a citizen of India who is a non-resident as defined in clause (30) of section 2 of the Income-tax Act, 1961; (c) a body corporate, association or organization— (i) not incorporated or registered in India; or (ii) incorporated or registered in India under any law for the time being in force which has any non-Indian participation in its share capital or management, shall obtain any biological resource occurring in India or knowledge associated thereto for research or for commercial utilization or for bio-survey and bio-utilization without previous approval of the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA Form I).
chunks.explanation: Any foreign company, foreign national, NRI, or Indian company having foreign equity/shareholding must obtain prior NBA approval (Form I) before accessing any Indian biological resource (herbs, plants, botanical extracts) for commercial utilization or research.

chunks.chapter: Chapter II: Regulation of Access to Biological Diversity
chunks.title: Application for Intellectual Property Rights (IPR Approval - NBA Form III)
chunks.legal_text: 1. No person shall apply for any intellectual property right, by whatever name called, in or outside India for any invention based on any research or information on a biological resource obtained from India without obtaining the previous approval of the National Biodiversity Authority before grant of such intellectual property right (NBA Form III). Provided that in case of patent application, permission of the National Biodiversity Authority may be obtained after the acceptance of the patent application but before the sealing of the patent by the patent authority concerned. 2. The National Biodiversity Authority may, while granting the approval under this section, impose benefit sharing fee or royalty or conditions on the commercial utilization of such rights.
chunks.explanation: Crucial for Ayurvedic innovators: Filing any patent (in India or abroad via PCT/US/EPO) based on Indian biological resources requires prior NBA approval in Form III. Without NBA approval, the patent cannot be sealed and is liable to opposition/revocation under Section 64(1)(p) of Patents Act.

chunks.chapter: Chapter II: Regulation of Access to Biological Diversity
chunks.title: Prior Intimation to State Biodiversity Board (SBB) by Indian Entities
chunks.legal_text: No person, who is a citizen of India or a body corporate, association or organization which is registered in India, shall obtain any biological resource for commercial utilization, or bio-survey and bio-utilization for commercial utilization except after giving prior intimation to the State Biodiversity Board concerned: Provided that the provisions of this section shall not apply to the local people and communities of the area, including growers and cultivators of biological resources, and vaids and hakims, who have been practicing indigenous medicine.
chunks.explanation: Indian companies and citizens must give prior intimation to the respective State Biodiversity Board (SBB) before commercially utilizing biological resources. SBB may levy access & benefit sharing (ABS) fees.

chunks.title: Normally Traded Commodities (NTAC) and Codified AYUSH Practitioner Exemptions
chunks.legal_text: Under Section 40, the Central Government exempts 421+ normally traded commodities (NTAC - agricultural crops and commodities traded for consumption) from the purview of the Act. Furthermore, under the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023: 1. Registered AYUSH practitioners, traditional healers (vaids and hakims), and cultivators of medicinal plants are explicitly exempt from ABS obligations when preparing medicines for their own clinical practice. 2. Codified traditional knowledge systems (Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani) recognized in the First Schedule to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act are exempt from ABS obligations for domestic Indian manufacturers, provided cultivated biological resources with traceability certificates are utilized.
chunks.explanation: Ayurvedic practitioners and growers are exempt from ABS, but commercial manufacturers using wild-collected biological resources or exporting abroad must comply with SBB/NBA regulations.

chunks.act_title: Guidelines on Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) Regulations
chunks.title: Calculation of Fair and Equitable Benefit Sharing (ABS Percentage)
chunks.legal_text: Benefit sharing obligations for commercial utilization of biological resources are calculated on the ex-factory sale price (minus government taxes): 1. Up to ₹1 Crore annual turnover: 0.1% of ex-factory price. 2. Between ₹1 Crore and ₹3 Crore annual turnover: 0.2% of ex-factory price. 3. Above ₹3 Crore annual turnover: 0.5% of ex-factory price. Alternatively, for buyer-trader transactions, benefit sharing is between 1% to 3% of the purchase price of biological resources. For IPR commercialization/licensing, benefit sharing ranges between 3.0% to 5.0% of the royalty or gross revenue generated from IPR licensing.
chunks.explanation: Commercial AYUSH companies must budget between 0.1% to 0.5% of ex-factory sales as statutory ABS payments remitted to State Biodiversity Boards or NBA.
